paragraphs: Xeris Biopharma Holdings, Inc. along with its subsidiaries, is referenced herein as the "Company", "Xeris", "Xeris Biopharma", "we" or "our". Throughout this document, unless otherwise noted, references to Gvoke include Gvoke PFS, Gvoke HypoPen, and Gvoke Kit.

We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for people with chronic endocrine and neurological diseases in the United States. We offer Recorlev for the treatment of endogenous hypercortisolemia in patients with Cushing's syndrome, Gvoke for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia, and Keveyis for the treatment of Primary Periodic Paralysis ("PPP"). We are advancing our Phase 3-ready pipeline product, XP-8121, once-weekly subcutaneous ("SC") levothyroxine, which leverages our proprietary technology XeriSol.
Our top priority is maximizing the potential of our three commercial products:

•Recorlev is a cortisol synthesis inhibitor approved for the treatment of endogenous hypercortisolemia in adults with Cushing's syndrome for whom surgery is not an option or has not been curative. Endogenous Cushing's syndrome is a rare but serious and potentially fatal endocrine disease caused by chronic elevated cortisol exposure. Recently published data has shown that hypercortisolemia may be a contributor to several widespread and chronic medical conditions suggesting that the prevalence of the condition may be significantly higher than previously believed. We believe this therapy represents a significant commercial opportunity in the United States, with the potential to generate approximately $1 billion in annual net revenue at peak penetration.

•Gvoke is a ready-to-use, liquid-stable glucagon for the treatment of severe hypoglycemia. The product is indicated for use in pediatric and adult patients with diabetes age two years and above and can be administered in two simple steps. We estimate that more than 14 million people in the United States are at heightened risk of severe hypoglycemia and, per guidelines issued by the American Diabetes Association and others, should have a ready-to-use glucagon product like the Gvoke HypoPen with them at all times. The estimated total addressable market for this drug is approximately $5.0 billion in the United States.

•Keveyis is the first therapy approved in the United States to treat hyperkalemic, hypokalemic, and related variants of PPP. PPP is a rare genetic, neuromuscular disorder that can cause extreme muscle weakness and/or paralysis; some forms are also commonly associated with myotonia or muscle stiffness. The estimated total addressable market for this therapy is greater than $0.5 billion in the United States.

We prioritize our development efforts on programs that leverage our commercial capabilities or our proprietary formulation technologies, principally our lead pipeline program, XP-8121. Our company name, Xeris, is derived from the ancient Greek word xērós meaning 'dry' or 'without water/non-aqueous'. Our proprietary, non-aqueous formulations are designed to enable the convenient injection of medicines previously uninjectable or poorly injectable when utilizing aqueous approaches. XeriSol and XeriJect offer the opportunity to create ready-to-use, room-temperature stable, highly concentrated, injectable formulations of both small and large molecules.

•XP-8121: We are in the process of developing the first and only, once-weekly, subcutaneous injection of levothyroxine for the treatment of hypothyroidism. We plan to initiate a Phase 3 clinical trial of XP-8121 in 2026. The estimated total addressable market for this therapy is 3-5 million patients or more in the United States which we estimate is a $1.0 to $3.0 billion peak net sales opportunity.

•Partnerships: We are pursuing formulation and development partnerships to apply our XeriSol and XeriJect formulation technologies to enhance the drug delivery and clinical profile of other companies' proprietary drugs and biologics. Currently, Xeris is working on a number of formulation feasibility programs in the areas of small molecules, peptides, biologics and monoclonal antibodies.

Our strategy is to build a profitable biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for people with chronic endocrine and neurological diseases. Xeris is uniquely positioned to execute on this strategy through the continued growth of our three commercial products, which enables us to invest in and develop therapies for unmet medical needs. We believe this will generate value for all of our stakeholders.

Recorlev, approved in 2022, is our therapy for the treatment of Cushing's syndrome, a rare condition which is the result of sustained, elevated levels of cortisol in the body (hypercortisolism). Cushing's syndrome affects approximately 25,000 people in the United States of which approximately two-thirds are cured by surgery. Pharmacologic products like Recorlev are used for the balance of patients for whom surgery was not curative or was not an option. Recorlev has received orphan drug exclusivity status in the United States through December 30, 2028 and patent protection through 2040.

We believe this therapy represents a significant commercial opportunity within the United States, having the potential to generate approximately $1 billion in annual net revenue at peak penetration. Recorlev competes primarily with other established medications and therapies, including older generic drugs that are used off-label for Recorlev's approved indication. Because of the complex nature of Cushing's syndrome, many patients are inadequately treated with currently available medicines.

Our experienced commercial organization focuses on educating prescribing clinicians and patients to raise awareness of the benefits of normalizing cortisol with Recorlev. Our Xeris' CareConnection program provides direct, dedicated support to treating clinicians and patients throughout their Recorlev journey. In addition, our efforts include the support of a single, highly experienced specialty pharmacy that provides logistical assistance in the securing of coverage from third-party payors and then subsequent distribution of Recorlev to patients.

Gvoke is our ready-to-use, room-temperature stable, liquid glucagon product. Available since late 2019, Gvoke is a potentially life-saving rescue product that is designated to be reliably administrated by the individual with diabetes or their caregivers during low blood sugar emergencies (e.g., a severe hypoglycemic episode). Gvoke is available in three presentation types: Gvoke HypoPen (auto-injector), Gvoke PFS (pre-filled syringe), and Gvoke Kit (pre-filled vial and administration syringe). Our most widely prescribed presentation, Gvoke HypoPen, is designed to be administered subcutaneously in a simple two-step process requiring no dose calibration. Gvoke has patent protection through 2036.

headings: Risks Related to our Financial Position and Need for Financing
We have a limited operating history and limited experience commercializing pharmaceutical products and have incurred significant losses since inception.
We have a history of operating losses and may not be able to achieve or sustain profitability in the future, and we may not be able to continue operations without additional fundings.

Risks Related to the Commercialization and Marketing of our Products and Product Candidates

Our business depends entirely on the commercial success of our products and product candidates. Even if approved, our product candidates may not be accepted in the marketplace and our business may be materially harmed.

We are party to a number of material agreements which contain complex commercial terms that could result in litigation or liability that could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the following risk factors, in evaluating us and our business. If any of the following risks and uncertainties actually occurs, our business, prospects, financial condition and results of operations could be materially and adversely affected. The risks summarized and described below are not intended to be exhaustive and are not the only risks facing us. New risk factors can emerge from time to time, and it is not possible to predict the impact that any factor or combination of factors may have on our business, prospects, financial condition and results of operations. You should also consider the other information included in this Annual Report as well as our other filings with the SEC.

Historically, we have funded our operations primarily through private placements of convertible preferred stock, public offerings of common stock and convertible notes, and debt issuances. We have five pharmaceutical products that have been commercially launched over the past several years, i.e., Keveyis (2017), Gvoke PFS (2019), Gvoke HypoPen (2020), Recorlev (2022), and Gvoke Kit (2022). We are in the early stages of commercializing our biopharmaceutical products and have a limited operating history.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we reported net income of $0.6 million. For the years ended December 31, 2024 and 2023, we reported net losses of $54.8 million and $62.3 million, respectively. In addition, our accumulated deficit as of December 31, 2025 was $671.3 million.

We are a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for people with chronic endocrine and neurological diseases in the United States. We are advancing our Phase 3-ready pipeline product, XP-8121, once-weekly subcutaneous ("SC") levothyroxine, which leverages our proprietary technology XeriSol.
We have funded our operations to date primarily with proceeds from the sale of our common stock and debt financing.

The year ended December 31, 2025 is the first year we have been profitable since inception, and, as of December 31, 2025, our accumulated deficit was $671.3 million. In the near term, we may incur net losses as we:
< continue our marketing and selling efforts related to commercialization of Recorlev, Gvoke and Keveyis;
< continue our research and development efforts; < continue to operate as a public company; and

We may continue to seek public equity and debt financing to meet our capital requirements. There can be no assurance that such funding may be available to us on acceptable terms, or at all, or that we will be able to commercialize our product candidates, if approved. In addition, we may not be profitable even if we commercialize any of our product candidates.
The following discussion sets forth certain components of the statement of operations of Xeris for the year ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 as well as factors that impact those items.

Product revenue, net, represents gross product sales less estimated allowances for patient copay assistance programs, prompt payment discounts, payor rebates, chargebacks, service fees, and product returns, all of which are recorded at the time of sale to the pharmaceutical wholesaler or other customer. We apply significant judgment and estimates in determining some of these allowances. If actual results differ from our estimates, we make adjustments to these allowances in the period in which the actual results or updates to estimates become known.

Royalty and contract revenue is recognized as earned in accordance with contract terms when it can be reasonably estimated and collectability is reasonably assured. Revenue generated from various collaboration and technology partnerships are included in this line item.

Cost of goods sold primarily includes product costs, which include all costs directly related to the purchase of raw materials, charges from our contract manufacturing organizations, and manufacturing overhead costs, as well as shipping and distribution charges. Cost of goods sold also includes losses from excess, slow-moving or obsolete inventory and inventory purchase commitments, if any.

Research and development expenses consist of expenses incurred in connection with the discovery and development of our products and product candidates. We recognize research and development expenses as incurred. Expenses that are paid in advance of performance are capitalized until services are provided or goods are delivered. paragraphs: Xeris Biopharma Holdings, Inc. 以及其子公司，於本文件中被稱為 "Company"、"Xeris"、"Xeris Biopharma"、"we" 或 "our"。於本文件中，除非另有說明，提及 Gvoke 時包括 Gvoke PFS、Gvoke HypoPen 以及 Gvoke Kit。

我們是一家商業階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發與商業化用以治療美國患有慢性內分泌及神經系統疾病的患者的療法。我們提供 Recorlev 用以治療庫欣症候羣患者的內源性高皮質醇血癥，Gvoke 用以治療嚴重低血糖，以及 Keveyis 用以治療原發性週期性癱瘓（"PPP"）。我們正在推進我們的 Phase 3 就緒產品 XP-8121，這是一款每週一次皮下（"SC"）給予的左旋甲狀腺素，該產品利用我們的專有技術 XeriSol。
我們的首要目標是最大化我們三個商業產品的潛力：
•Gvoke 是一種即用型、液體穩定的胰高血糖素，用以治療嚴重低血糖。此產品核准用於年齡兩歲以上之糖尿病患者，包括兒童及成人，且可透過兩步驟簡單給予。我們估計美國有超過 14 百萬人處於嚴重低血糖風險中，根據美國糖尿病協會及其他機構所發佈的指引，這些人應隨時攜帶如 Gvoke HypoPen 這類即用型胰高血糖素產品。此藥物的總可達市場估計為美國約 5.0 十億美元。
•Keveyis 是美國首個核准用以治療高血鉀性、低血鉀性及相關變異型 PPP 的療法。PPP 是一種罕見的遺傳性、神經肌肉疾病，可能導致極度肌肉無力或癱瘓；某些形式也常與肌束震顫或肌肉僵硬相關。此療法的總可達市場估計為美國超過 0.5 十億美元。

我們的開發努力優先考量那些能利用我們商業能力或專有製劑技術的計畫，主要為我們的領先產品線計畫 XP-8121。我們公司的名稱 Xeris 來自古希臘語 xērós，意為 "乾燥" 或 "無水/非水性"。我們的專有非水性製劑設計用以實現先前無法注射或注射困難的藥物，透過水性方法來注射。XeriSol 和 XeriJect 提供機會，製造即用型、室溫穩定、高度濃縮、可注射的製劑，適用於小分子與大分子。
•XP-8121：我們正在開發第一款且唯一一款每週一次皮下注射的左旋甲狀腺素，用以治療甲狀腺功能低下。我們計畫於 2026 年啟動 XP-8121 的 Phase 3 臨牀試驗。此療法的總可達市場估計為美國 3-5 百萬名患者或更多，我們估計這是一個 1.0 到 3.0 十億美元的峯值淨銷售機會。
•策略合作夥伴關係：我們正在尋求與合作夥伴進行配方與開發合作，以應用我們的 XeriSol 和 XeriJect 配方技術，以提升其他公司專利藥物與生物製劑的藥物遞送效能與臨牀表現。目前，Xeris 正在進行多項配方可行性計畫，範疇包括小分子、肽類、生物製劑與單克隆抗體。
我們的策略是建立一家獲利的生物製藥公司，專注於開發與商業化治療慢性內分泌與神經系統疾病的療法。Xeris 透過持續成長我們的三個商業產品，獨特地具備執行此策略的能力，使我們得以投資並開發未被滿足的醫療需求。我們相信這將為我們所有利害關係人創造價值。

Recorlev 於 2022 年獲准上市，是我們用以治療庫興症候羣（Cushing's syndrome）的療法，一種罕見的疾病，其成因為體內持續高於正常水平的皮質醇（hypercortisolism）。庫興症候羣在美國約影響 25,000 人，其中約三分之二的患者透過手術可被治癒。類藥物製品如 Recorlev 會用於治療那些手術未治癒或無法接受手術的患者。Recorlev 已經獲得美國罕見疾病藥物獨佔權，至 2028 年 12 月 30 日為止，並享有至 2040 年的專利保護。
我們經驗豐富的商業團隊專注於教育處方醫師與患者，提高對以 Recorlev 正常化皮質醇的益處的認知。我們的 Xeris CareConnection 計畫為治療醫師與患者提供直接且專屬的支援，協助他們在 Recorlev 的治療過程中。此外，我們的努力也包括支持一家單一且經驗豐富的專門藥房，提供在取得第三方付款者覆蓋方面的物流協助，並隨後將 Recorlev 分配給患者。

Gvoke 是我們的即用型、室溫穩定、液態胰島素製品。自 2019 年末上市以來，Gvoke 是一種可能挽救生命的急救產品，設計為在糖尿病患者或其照顧者於低血糖緊急情況（例如嚴重低血糖發作）時可靠地使用。Gvoke 有三種呈現形式：Gvoke HypoPen（自動注射器）、Gvoke PFS（預灌封針筒）以及 Gvoke Kit（預灌封小瓶與注射針筒）。我們最常被處方的呈現形式 Gvoke HypoPen，設計為透過簡單的兩步驟過程皮下注射，無需劑量校準。Gvoke 的專利保護至 2036 年。

headings: 與本公司財務狀況相關的風險及資金需求
本公司營運歷史有限且商業化藥物產品的經驗有限，自成立以來已產生重大虧損。
本公司有營運虧損的歷史，未來可能無法達成或維持獲利，且可能無法在未獲得額外資金的情況下持續營運。
高於預期的產品退貨可能超過本公司針對退貨所提列的備抵金額。
與產品商業化及行銷相關的風險及產品候選藥物
本公司業務完全依賴產品及產品候選藥物的商業成功。即使獲得核准，產品候選藥物也可能不被市場接受，進而對本公司業務造成重大損害。
本公司為數個重要契約的一方，這些契約包含複雜的商業條款，可能導致訴訟或責任，進而對本公司業務、營運成果及財務狀況造成不利影響。

歷史上，本公司主要透過私募可轉換優先股、公開發行普通股與可轉換票據，以及發行債務來資助營運。本公司過去幾年已商業化五項藥物產品，即 Keveyis（2017 年）、Gvoke PFS（2019 年）、Gvoke HypoPen（2020 年）、Recorlev（2022 年）以及 Gvoke Kit（2022 年）。本公司目前處於生物製藥產品商業化的初期階段，且營運歷史有限。
會計年度終了為 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司報出淨收入為 0.6 百萬美元。會計年度終了為 2024 年 12 月 31 日及 2023 年 12 月 31 日，本公司分別報出淨虧損為 54.8 百萬美元及 62.3 百萬美元。此外，本公司截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日累計虧損為 671.3 百萬美元。
